audit.why: 53.89% over 488 games, diff FAV at 4/10 with carryRating 5/10. This page is already far above the repo average — it has per-phase reasoning rather than boilerplate, and the difficulty read matches the number.

Both layers read Olaf on all seven rows and the packet chart agrees on all seven. No split between phases[N].side and win[N]. Ratings taper sensibly (8,8,8,8,7,6,7) rather than sitting flat, correctly marking his Lich Bane window as Olaf's weakest row.
audit.corrected: No change needed — this is the only chart in my slice that was already correct in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction of this matchup is absent from every string. Reckless Swing deals its true damage by costing Olaf health, Berserker Rage makes Olaf stronger the lower he is, and Locke's passive deals bonus magic damage 'increased based on enemy missing Health' feeding an ultimate that executes. Olaf's entire optimal state — low HP, swinging — is precisely Locke's kill condition. Two smaller errors: whys[1] credits the W with lifesteal (Riot's W text is attack speed plus a shield; the lifesteal is the passive), and whys[4] says Ragnarok 'deletes his slows', where Riot's text grants immunity to disables only, and only while Olaf keeps attacking.
audit.why: Everything else on this page tells the player to fight low and keep swinging — which is correct against most champions and actively suicidal near a 120-second execute that scales off missing health. Without this stated, a player follows good general Olaf advice straight into the one build Locke is designed to punish. This is the fact that turns the page's own 'never fight at sliver HP inside Purgatory' from a rule into a reason.
audit.corrected: Created the missing spikes[3] entry to carry the interaction explicitly, and pointed whys[6] at it. whys[1] now credits Berserker Rage; whys[4] now says Ragnarok blanks disables while you keep swinging.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's cooldown discipline is genuinely good — it repeatedly names the ten seconds after a spent E, which matches the kit's flat 10s cooldown exactly. But Purgatory's 120/100/80s never appears.
audit.why: The advice 'disengage above his floor' is open-ended without a number. 120 seconds at rank 1 is a long stretch in which the execute simply is not a consideration, and the player should be told they can fight freely in it.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns now carry the 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].t reads 'Dive him at low HP with his totem down'. Everywhere else on the page 'down' means on cooldown, and a totem on cooldown is the page's own recommended dive window — report[9].t says to commit 'with your jungler when his totem is down'.
audit.why: As written, the Critical Don'ts list forbids the exact play the All-In Windows section recommends. One of the two is inverted, and the kit says the dangerous state is Purgatory being available.

notes: Best-written page in my slice by some margin — the chart was already correct in both layers, the ten-second post-E window matches the kit's flat 10s E exactly, and report[8] correctly identifies his W sustain as a self-refund rather than lifesteal, so anti-heal is correctly called optional. Two things I did NOT change because I cannot verify them from the kit: the ability names. The brief's packet.enemyAbilities is null for Locke and the kit entries carry no name field, so 'Ritual Nails', 'Ashen Pursuit' and 'Purgatory' are unconfirmed — the only naming evidence anywhere in the data is Riot's Q text, which says he 'readies a set of Soul Nails'. That is a possible Brand/Pyroclasm-class error, but it is equally possible Soul Nails is the projectile and Ritual Nails the ability, so I left every name alone. I also left the repeated '125 range' claim: nothing in the kit gives his attack range. breakdown.cooldowns previously said his E 'resets on takedowns', which is not in Riot's E text either — I removed that clause when adding the 10s rather than assert it.
